children: Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, climb due to inflation concerns as Brent crude trades above $107 a barrel. High oil prices have caused markets to raise their expectations of the Bank of England increasing interest rates in the coming months. The latest U.K. jobs data show the unemployment rate stayed unchanged at 4.9% in the three months to July. The estimate of payrolled employees also decreased by 26,000 between July and August. Despite the weak jobs data, U.K. gilt yields are likely to remain elevated due to the global trend of rising bond yields, Aberdeen's Felix Feather says in a note. U.K. 10-year gilt yields climb 0.9 basis point to last trade at 5.410%, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
